chunks: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Taleqani (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Abu Sa'id al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Adavi narrated that Sahib ibn Abbad narrated that his father narrated from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his grandfather (peace be upon them):

He said: Pleasure (al-nushwah) is in ten things: walking, riding, swimming in water, looking at greenery, eating and drinking, sexual intercourse, using the siwak (tooth-cleaning twig), washing the head with mallow, looking at a beautiful woman, and conversing with men.

key_terms.السِّوَاك: Using a tooth-cleaning twig for oral hygiene
key_terms.النُّشْوَة: Pleasure, refreshment, or lightness of spirit
key_terms.الْخُطْمِيّ: Mallow plant, used here for washing the head

ai.seo_question: What are the ten things that bring pleasure according to Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Compiled by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Al-Khisal*, this hadith from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) categorizes ten sources of 'nushwah' (refreshment/pleasure) that sustain human well-being, ranging from physical acts like walking and swimming to sensory delights like viewing greenery and beauty. It reflects the Shia ethical principle of *mubahat* (permissibility), affirming that worldly pleasures are not merely tolerated but are divinely ordained means of spiritual and physical rejuvenation when enjoyed within moderation.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 10-39 Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Taleqani - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Abu Sa’id al-Hassan ibn Ali al-Adavi quoted Saheeb ibn Ebad, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ja’far ibn Muhammad as-Sadiq (MGB), on the authority of his father (MGB), on the authority of his grandfather (MGB),

“There is pleasure in ten things: walking, riding, swimming, looking at greenery, eating and drinking, having sexual intercourse, brushing your teeth, washing one’s head with mallow, looking at beautiful women, and associating with other men.”
